newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine shares end up after choppy session.
newsitem.headline: Philippine shares end up after choppy session.

text.p: Recovering property stocks nudged the Philippine stock index higher at Wednesday's close amidst a generally cautious market, traders said.

"It was the property sector that's up, but people are really on a wait-and-see with the Hong Kong handover barely six days away and with the Federal Reserve meeting once again," said Jonathan Ravelas, head of sales at Asian Capital Equities.
The main index ended 11.02 points up, or 0.39 percent, to 2,829.29 points, after falling to its intra-day low of 2,810.13 by midsession.
The market was initially cheered by the hefty gains in Wall Street, but profit-takers briefly reigned by midsession. A wave of late bargain hunting finally lifted the index at close.
Turnover was moderate at 2.2 billion pesos. Losers pounced gainers 73 to 38 with 75 issues unchanged.
Ayala Land was the most actively traded issue, closing 75 centavos higher at 23.75 pesos.
Other blue chip issues that helped lift the market were Benpres Holdings Corp, Pilipino Telephone Corp and PLDT.
Anscor-Hagedorn Securities vice-president Noel Reyes added he expected volume to dwindle ahead of the Hong Kong handover, keeping most foreign fund managers out of the regional markets.
"I see a strong bearish to neutral sentiment given the fact that people are awaiting upcoming events such as the U.S. Fed meeting and the Hong Kong handover," Ravelas said.
